items.title: The derived tensor product of two perfect complexes is perfect
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for a ring R, if K and L are perfect objects of D(R) then so is K tensor^L_R L (source lines 19050-19054). The proof gives an elementary argument via the definition: representing K and L by bounded complexes K^bullet and L^bullet of finite projective R-modules, the derived tensor product is represented by the bounded total complex Tot(K^bullet tensor_R L^bullet) (proof lines 19056-19061). The substantive observation is that the terms of that complex are direct sums of the modules M^a tensor_R L^b, and since M^a and L^b are direct summands of finite free R-modules, so is their tensor product; hence the terms of the total complex are finite projective, which makes it a bounded complex of finite projective modules and therefore perfect (proof lines 19062-19066). The proof then records a second route: the characterisation of perfect complexes together with the corresponding statements for pseudo-coherent complexes and for tor amplitude, the latter applied with A = B = R (proof lines 19068-19073). The non-routine content is the closure of finite projectivity under tensor products of summands of finite free modules, which is what makes the total complex eligible.
